parsed.headline: Syria and Bangladesh condemn Houthi drone attack on Medina power station

pages.text: Syria’s Foreign Ministry condemned a Houthi drone attack on a power distribution station in Medina, Saudi Arabia, stating the strike targeted civilian infrastructure. According to the North Press Agency, the ministry said the attack on the station, which supplies electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque, violated Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and threatened regional stability. A Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis stated the group recently attacked the power distribution station in Medina. On September 27, 2026, the government of Bangladesh also issued a condemnation regarding the strike on the Taibah electricity station. The Bangladeshi Ministry of Foreign Affairs described the targeting of infrastructure serving the Prophet's Mosque as an unacceptable assault on the sanctity of Islam's holiest sites. Bangladesh stated it stands in solidarity with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and rejected acts of aggression that harm regional peace and stability.

parsed.headline: UAE prosecutor says Flydubai co-pilot used crash axe in attempted terrorist attack

pages.text: United Arab Emirates prosecutor general Hamad Saif al-Shamsi stated on Saturday that the co-pilot of Flydubai flight FZ1073 used a crash axe to attempt a “terrorist attack” during a flight bound for Israel. The incident occurred on September 30, 2026, when the aircraft, carrying 182 people, plunged 16,625 feet in just over 30 seconds. Passengers and crew intervened to stop the co-pilot's attempt to take control of the plane, and two reserve pilots subsequently landed the aircraft safely in Saudi Arabia. The extreme descent resulted in part of the plane's rudder being ripped off. The Flydubai captain, Indian national Smit Machchhar, sustained wounds to his head, hands, and neck during the attack. Machchhar reported that while lying injured on the floor, he used his remaining energy to unlock the cockpit door from the inside, allowing passengers and crew to enter, subdue the attacker, and stabilize the aircraft. The Indian government has praised Machchhar for his courage during the event.

Media outlets have identified the co-pilot as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, though there has been no official confirmation of this identity from the UAE or Flydubai. Reports from the Wall Street Journal and the Associated Press indicate that Al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying by Oman due to concerns regarding extremist views, after which he was moved to an administrative role at Oman Air before being hired by Flydubai. Investigations are ongoing to determine if the individual acted as a “lone wolf” or had connections to extremist groups. On October 2, 2026, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radicalization,” though he provided no evidence. While early passenger reports suggested a knife may have been used, Al-Shamsi clarified that the weapon used was a crash axe, an implement typically kept inside the cockpit for emergencies such as fires or crashes. Security agencies from four regional countries, including Israel, are working with the United States and other Western governments to establish motives.

parsed.headline: Stakeholders call for National Political History and Heritage Centre in Saltpond, Ghana

pages.text: Ernest De-Graft Egyir, President of the Mfantseman-Saltpond Development Alliance (MSDA), has called for the establishment of a National Political History and Heritage Centre in Saltpond, Ghana. Speaking at a Founders’ Day commemoration themed “Saltpond Heritage, Ghana’s Future, Turning History into Opportunity,” Egyir proposed that the center be used to preserve the country's political history and transform local historic sites into opportunities for tourism, research, education, and economic development. He suggested the institution should document Ghana's transition from colonial rule to independence by preserving political archives, oral histories, photographs, and other records related to the independence struggle. Egyir stated the initiative should be national rather than partisan, seeking to represent the various movements and people involved in independence without being tied to the NDC or NPP political parties. He further proposed linking the center to a wider heritage corridor to connect historical sites with hospitality, local enterprise, and tourism. As part of the potential heritage development, Egyir cited Canaan Lodge, the site where the United Gold Coast Convention (UGCC) was launched on August 4, 1947. Egyir called for support from the government, the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, the Ghana Tourism Authority, traditional authorities, universities, historians, the private sector, development partners, and the diaspora.

parsed.headline: Brazilian presidential election presents potential shift in Amazon rainforest policies

pages.text: The upcoming presidential election in Brazil could reshape the future of the Amazon rainforest, which accounts for approximately 60% of the ecosystem. Experts have warned that a victory by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, could reverse deforestation-control policies that were restored by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. During the presidency of Jair Bolsonaro, Amazon deforestation increased by about 60%. In 2023, President Lula reinstated an anti-deforestation plan that reduced deforestation by 45%. Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to end illegal deforestation by 2029, though he has not provided details on how this goal would be achieved. Concerns persist regarding the potential weakening of environmental protections.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh Minister calls for innovation ecosystem to transition to technology producer

pages.text: Speaking at the Bangladesh ICT and Innovation Awards 2026 at BRAC University in Dhaka, Bangladesh Science and Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam stated on Saturday that the country must move beyond consuming foreign technology to developing its own research and technological capabilities. The minister said the goal is to become a producer and exporter of technology, ICT, and telecom. He noted that the government is working to establish a “Made in Bangladesh” brand in sectors including software, semiconductor design, artificial intelligence, digital services, and data centres. To achieve a $1 trillion economy by 2034, Anam said greater emphasis must be placed on a knowledge-based economy and research alongside manufacturing-led growth. He also stated the country aims to strengthen its position as a leading digital economy within five years by transitioning from a labour-intensive to a knowledge-based economy.

Science and Technology Secretary Md Anwar Hossain noted that while Bangladesh has relatively good research infrastructure, it faces limitations in commercialisation, incubation, and marketing. Hossain said the government is working to create an innovation-friendly environment, as the country currently lacks effective links between government, industry, and academia. He added that skilled human resources, financing, and policy support are necessary to convert research into social and economic impact. According to Hossain, work is underway regarding tax support for research and development, access to finance, intellectual property protection, and policy support for importing modern research equipment. Additionally, the first Bangladesh Innovation Fair 2026 was cited as a platform that brought together academia, industry, financial institutions, investors, and innovators.

parsed.headline: Brazil presidential election pits incumbent Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro

pages.text: On September 27, 2026, Brazil held a presidential election featuring a neck-and-neck race between 80-year-old leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and 45-year-old far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Lula is seeking a fourth non-consecutive term, while Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to join the Shield of the Americas—an anti-drug cartel coalition of 15 countries governed by right or far-right leaders—and adopt an “iron fist” approach to crime. Lula has expressed concerns regarding sovereignty and criticized the “inferiority complex” of Latin American presidents participating in the Trump-created coalition. The candidates differ on U.S. foreign policy, specifically the “war on drugs” which has involved joint land operations and airstrikes on boats that have killed more than 230 people.

The election follows a period in which U.S. President Donald Trump claimed that right-wing candidates had won all seven presidential elections held in the region since the start of his second term. According to The Guardian World, the U.S. takeover of Venezuela following the capture of Nicolás Maduro has left only six Latin American countries under left-wing governments: Brazil, Mexico, Uruguay, Guatemala, Cuba, and Nicaragua. Pedro Telles, a professor at Brazil’s FGV university, noted that if Flávio Bolsonaro wins, it could provide a boost to the global far-right agenda. Sandra Borda Guzmán, an associate professor of political science at Colombia’s Universidad de los Andes, stated that a far-right victory would align the region unconditionally with U.S. dictates rather than expanding regional autonomy.

parsed.headline: Olivia Chow pledges free family programming if re-elected in Toronto

pages.text: Toronto mayoral candidate Olivia Chow has promised to implement more free programming for families if re-elected. During campaigning on Saturday, Chow pledged to provide free weekend programming for children at public libraries. Additionally, Chow proposed expanding the Toronto Public Library program tpl:map by 1,000 new passes, which offers free family admission to local museums and attractions.
